name: BattleAi_PickRandomTargetAboveDamage
signature: void* BattleAi_PickRandomTargetAboveDamage(void* aiCtx, u32 skillId, void* preferredTarget)
summary: Battle-AI target picker: walks the 16 candidate buckets at aiCtx+0x10 (stride 0x9BC), keeps units that are alive and accept the skill (vtable slots +0x18/+0xF8/+0xFC with SkillRecord->u8_e2), estimates damage with Battle_ApplyDamageClamp, and returns one of the units whose damage exceeds the AiRecord threshold at +0x147, chosen with the battle RNG; falls back to the preferred target.
evidence: Both callers are confirmed battle-AI selection code: BattleAi_FilterUsableCandidates (0x0027240C) and BattleAi_SelectActionForMode (0x00637BDC). The skill record is resolved with the confirmed SkillRecord wrapper 0x0018C1B8 and the pick uses the battle RNG through func_001CA474, exactly as the FACTS describe for BattleAi_* candidate evaluation.

name: Field2D_Object_NeedsUpdate
summary: Per-frame gate for a Field2D object: returns 1 (still needs processing) unless the interface at self+0x88 answers 0 and both idle queries func_00669B68/func_00669B7C on *(self+8) report non-zero (i.e. the object is fully idle).
evidence: Callers Field2D_Scene_RenderObjects (0x005C5F24), txf (0x005C73D8) and Field2D_JumpTableEntry4 (0x005CB3BC) use it per object before rendering/updating, so the polarity (1 = object is not idle) matches the name; only the interface at +0x88 remains unnamed.

name: Field2D_Object_NeedsUpdateB
summary: Same per-frame gate as 0x00667AE8, dispatching through the interface pointer at self+0xA0 instead of +0x88 (two interface variants of the same Field2D object class); returns 1 unless the interface and both idle queries all report idle.
evidence: Body is instruction-for-instruction the same as 0x00667AE8 apart from the +0xA0 load; same callers Field2D_Scene_RenderObjects (0x005C5F24) and txf (0x005C73D8). The 'B' suffix is a deliberate duplicate marker (template copy), not a different meaning.

name: maybe_Ipc_OpenSessionAndSend
signature: u32 maybe_Ipc_OpenSessionAndSend(u32* handleOut, u32 name, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, int value, u32 flags, int third)
summary: Lazily opens the DSP/nn service session (name length via 0x0011CCA0, open via 0x001192C0; failure returns 0xD92103FB) and then runs the shared locked request path: sets the command word, takes the session lock, sends, and signals. Ghidra dropped two register arguments, so the send argument list is incomplete.
evidence: Body is damaged (software_interrupt 0x23, linkValue/ownerPtr fragments, unaff_ registers) and the send tail is shared with 0x0011E9C4, so only the open-session half is trustworthy; the two callers (Svc_Cfg_OpenServiceS/I) are themselves maybe_. Kept as maybe_ per FACTS.md Ghidra traps.

name: maybe_Ipc_OpenSessionTailFragment
signature: u32 maybe_Ipc_OpenSessionTailFragment(u32 pad, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Ghidra-seeded fragment (54 bytes, thumb) that is really the shared send tail of the 0x0011E940/0x0011E9C4 cluster: takes g_dspServiceMutex, calls Svc_IpcCmd1100C2Read on the session pointer and signals the semaphore; returns 0xC8A0A7FC when the session is not connected. Not a real function start.
evidence: The '40 callers' are the whole Snd_* channel API, i.e. the address is used as an interior label, not a call target; the body is damaged (in_CY/in_ZR/in_OV, maybe_outPtrR6) and repeats the 0x0011E9C4 send path verbatim. Correctly identified as a mid-routine fragment.

name: Snd_Dsp_SendCommand1100C2
signature: u32 Snd_Dsp_SendCommand1100C2(u32 cmdArg0, u32 cmdArg1, u32 cmdArg2, u32 cmdArg3)
summary: Sends DSP-service command 0x1100C2 on the open nn session: spins on g_dspServiceMutex via func_001180B0, calls Svc_IpcCmd1100C2Read with the session pointer plus the caller's four command words, signals the semaphore, and returns 0xC8A0A7FC when the session is not connected.
evidence: All three callers are SND channel flush/wait paths (maybe_Snd_InitDspTimeouts 0x001071AC, maybe_Snd_FlushChannels 0x00118788, maybe_Snd_FlushChannelsOnStop 0x0011ECC0), which shows this is the sound subsystem's wrapper on the DSP session, not a raw SVC stub; the old Svc_ prefix suggested a libctru-style SVC wrapper that this is not (it locks a mutex and checks a global service state).

name: maybe_Scene_UpdateInterpolatedTransforms
summary: Large (3256-byte, damaged) per-frame helper: picks one of three controller slots at self+0xC, switches the active slot through vtable slots +0x18/+0x0C/+0x08, copies the previous/current transform pair (f_40 <- f_48, f_44 <- f_4C) and integrates the frame delta into the accumulated offsets before publishing them to the shared records. The tail contains std::container churn (rb-tree rebalance, Container_ResizeArray), so it is a template instance as much as a scene helper.
evidence: Callers span unrelated subsystems (Field_InitSceneObjects 0x0019CD50, Ui_SceneFlow_Update 0x0019E45C, Actor_Action_Trail_Start 0x004CD3E8 and Actor_Action_Trail_InitSamples 0x004CD664), which rules out the old 'Camera' attribution; the body is damaged (six unreachable-block warnings, heritage restart) so the name stays maybe_.

name: Ui_SceneFlow_UpdateCursorAndSprite
summary: Per-frame scene-flow step: lazily allocates and constructs the shared Ui_Core (0x98 bytes, vtable maybe_g_fieldSceneQueryTable), then, when Ui_ScreenTransition_IsBlockingDraw reports idle and the overlay is not in cursor mode, updates the selection cursor, and always advances the 2D sprite state for the current scene.
evidence: Sole caller is the confirmed Ui_SceneFlow_Update (0x0019E45C); the three callees Ui_ScreenTransition_IsBlockingDraw, maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateSelectionCursor and Field2D_Sprite_UpdateState are named, and the shared Ui_Core singleton is the same one used by the other Ui_SceneFlow helpers. Name describes exactly the two things it drives.

name: maybe_Ui_SlotTable_InitSubParts
summary: In-place constructor of three embedded sub-objects: func_002F2444 on self+0x5C, 0x003DACB0 (currently named Ui_SlotTable_UpdateSelection, used here as a ctor) on self+0x70, and returns the address of the third part at self+0xB8.
evidence: Shared by Ui_SceneFlow_Update (0x0019E45C) and the field-object ctor (0x001D6B90), so it is a generic three-sub-object initialiser rather than provably a UI slot table; the sub-object classes stay unnamed, so the Ui_ prefix and the SlotTable wording remain unproven.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_NutTask_Ctor
signature: u32* maybe_Actor_Action_NutTask_Ctor(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, const char* tag)

evidence: Callers include the already-named Actor_Action_Nut_Ctor (0x00373670) and Field_Action_Nut_Ctor (0x00301E14), so the nut family is right, but the same body is also reached from Model_AttachAccessoriesAndWeapons (0x0022E494) and a state-chain helper, i.e. it is a generic action-ctor tail; vtable/effect-id evidence only.

name: Field_ActorAction_BeginTurn
summary: Starts one turn of a field actor action: clears the action timer and turn-angle delta, snapshots the target actor transform into f_54/state-sequence node, and copies the attachment transform blocks from the current part (+0x5F4, identity when absent) into f_78..f_A4.
evidence: Sole caller is the confirmed Field_ActorAction_TurnStart (0x004137B8) and the function clears exactly the timers that Field_ActorAction_UpdateModelRotation later advances; 'Init' overstated it as a one-off constructor, while it runs once per turn.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_PlayStateEffect
signature: void maybe_Field_Object2D_PlayStateEffect(Field_Object2D* self, int state, u32 arg3, float scale)
summary: Forwards the state command to the children and to the model interface (vtable slot +0x38), and when entering state 10 or 11 releases the previous state effect handle and spawns effect 0x4B5 at the object position with the object orientation.
evidence: No callers at all, so neither the Field_Object2D class nor the 'state effect' reading can be confirmed; the effect id 0x4B5 and the state==10/11 gate are the only hard facts.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_BeginEffectState
summary: Entry into a visual effect state: clears the byte at +0x221; if the model-type byte at +0x8E is 0xFF it plays the fallback animation (0x0032DD6C) through vtable slot +0x84, otherwise it builds the spawn parameter block with the actor position and basis quaternion, spawns effect 0x45C and switches the actor to state 4 (vtable +0x40).
evidence: No callers and the spawn descriptor still has unnamed fields, so the class attribution stays a guess; effect 0x45C, the +0x8E == 0xFF test and the vtable +0x84 fallback are the concrete facts.

name: Field_Actor_PlaySituationEffect
summary: Plays the actor's type-dependent one-shot effect: if the busy byte at +0xB2 is clear it sets it, switches the actor to state 4 (vtable +0x58 and +0x40), clears +0xAD and spawns one of six effects (0x4CF/0x4D0/0x4D1/0x4D2/0x4D9/0x4D8) selected by the actor type byte at +0x2E5. Returns 1 when it started, 0 when already busy.
evidence: Whole body is intact (no unaff_/flag-register damage) and the effect-id switch plus the busy flag match the name; only the caller (maybe_Field_Actor_TriggerNearbySameType, 0x00371F6C) is still unnamed, so the 'situation' wording is a reasonable description of a type-keyed reaction effect.

name: Ui_Selector_BuildElevenRows
summary: Constructor-time builder of an eleven-row selector: loops i in 0..10 creating label+icon child panes (ui string ids 0x15+2i via func_002BCFF4, 'null_txt_l0'.. text panes through vtable +0x34/+0x38), then binds the 'select11' animation and resets the panes.
evidence: The eleven-iteration loop, the 'select11' animation literal and the Ui_AnimRef_Bind/ResetPanes callees are explicit; there is no caller, so 'selector' is the one remaining inference, but the function contains no other semantics.

name: maybe_Ui_DigitTable_Build
summary: Builds a ten-row digit pane table: binds the 'position1'/'position2' animations on the layout at window+0x98 and walks a decimal carry counter so each row gets the correctly incremented '..._r0_x'/'..._l0_x' pane name, then collects the named pane per row.
evidence: Only the literals 'position1'/'position2', the carry loop and the Ui_Window_CollectNamedPane callee are certain; 'Demo' in the old name came from nothing in the code and has been dropped, and there are no callers to identify the owning screen.

name: maybe_Ui_CommandList_BuildRows
summary: Constructor-time setup of a six-row list: registers the 'txt_title' pane and then, per row, an icon taken from g_uiPartyIconRowIndices (rows 0..8) plus a 'null_txt_l0'.. label pane, and finally selects row 0.
evidence: The party-icon index table g_uiPartyIconRowIndices ties the rows to party members, but nothing in the body says 'command'; there is no caller, so the list purpose stays unproven and the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ValuePanel_InitPanels
summary: Constructor-time setup of a three-slot panel: creates three 'null_txt_l0'.. text panes through vtable +0x38 and three sprite+label panes for UI string ids 0x5A, 0x5B and 0x70, then selects slot 0.
evidence: The three fixed ui string ids (0x5A/0x5B/0x70) show it is a specific screen panel, but no caller or string identifies which one, so 'ValuePanel' remains a description of the shape only.

name: maybe_Ui_PagedListWindow_InitPanes
signature: void maybe_Ui_PagedListWindow_InitPanes(void* window, void* layout, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Constructor-time initialiser of a paged four-column list: builds the 'txt_lN' index, 'txt_eN' name, 'txt_numN' number and 'txt_rN' right-value column panes with a decimal carry generator, plus the pager labels.
evidence: The four column-name families are hard evidence, but nothing mentions equipment (no item/equip record access anywhere in the body) and there is no caller, so the old EquipmentListWindow attribution is dropped in favour of a generic paged-list description.

name: maybe_Ui_NumberedListWindow_InitPanes
summary: Constructor-time initialiser of a long numbered list window: generates 28 'txt_lN' row labels with 'null_txt_l0'.. overlays through a decimal carry counter, then adds the pager and title labels.
evidence: Only generic numbered-list literals ('txt_l0'.., pager_num_l/r, txt_title_l) appear; no equipment or item record is touched and there is no caller, so the EquipmentListWindow prefix was unsupported and is replaced by a generic description.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_UpdateInteraction
summary: Per-frame step of a 2D field object: if it carries an actor handle (self+0x30) it resolves it through g_actorAttachGadgetHandleMap, accepts only actor type 0x20000001, binds it via func_00230A4C and asks the actor to play its idle animation; otherwise it sends command 0xB with mask 0xFFFFF800 through Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand and clears the sub-object.
evidence: Same handle-decode/attach code as 0x0040CFCC, so the object class is consistent, but no caller exists and command 0xB's meaning is unknown, hence 'Interaction' stays a description of the step rather than a proven role.

name: maybe_Actor_UpdateFollowTargetMotion
signature: void maybe_Actor_UpdateFollowTargetMotion(void* self, u32 handle, float dt)
summary: Computes the follow motion toward another actor: resolves the handle (type 0x20000001 only), builds the normalised direction between the two actors (SQRT + reciprocal), computes the reach distance as self radius + target height + 0.05 (0x3D4CCCCD) and blends the offset with acos-based angle math.
evidence: Sole caller is Field_SceneObject_SpawnByType (0x00352DBC), i.e. this runs at spawn rather than every frame, so the 'Update' part of the name is uncertain; the handle type mask, std_Acosf and the 0.05 reach constant are clear.

name: Field_Object2D_AttachToActor
summary: Binds the object to a live field actor: resolves the handle stored at self+0x30 through g_actorAttachGadgetHandleMap, accepts only type 0x20000001, registers self as the actor's gadget via func_00230A4C, starts the actor's idle animation and caches the bind word at self+0x2CC.
evidence: Clean body (no damaged registers) with the exact handle/type-mask prologue of the sibling 0x0040D1B8, which calls the same func_00230A4C + Actor_TryPlayIdleAnimation pair on the same object layout; only the absence of callers keeps it at 0.5.

name: maybe_Gfx_Node_ApplyTransformFromHandle
summary: Resolves the render handle at self+0x30 through g_actorAttachGadgetHandleMap (type 0x20000001), builds the world transform from self position + self rotation and pushes it into the object either as a 3D state change (func_00234014) or through the state-4 path (maybe_Gfx_Object_EnterState4); always returns 0.
evidence: The body contains no battle-sequence state machine, so the old Battle_Sequence_ prefix was wrong; it is the same handle-map + transform pattern as the field 2D objects (0x0040CFCC / 0x0040D1B8). No callers, so the class stays unproven.

name: maybe_BattleUi_SyncUnitListToLiveUnits
signature: void maybe_BattleUi_SyncUnitListToLiveUnits(void* self, int actionId, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Reconciles a battle unit list with the live units: walks the list at self+0x400, marks a list node live when its class matches a unit returned by the battle UI accessor (vtable +0x48), resolves the node's actor handle (type base g_actorBaseClass), and refreshes the unit text slots / list float parameters afterwards.
evidence: Damaged decompilation: the symbol starts at the interior label LAB_004262d8 of the surrounding routine and carries unaff_/in_ registers and duplicated dead blocks, so only the callee set (Battle_UnitList_SetActorsFloatParam 0x002AB8C0, Battle_RefreshUnitTextSlots 0x00428F68) is trustworthy; the old FinishUnitSelection/MenuClose guesses were invented.

name: maybe_BattleUi_UnitListTailFragment
signature: void maybe_BattleUi_UnitListTailFragment(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Not a real function: 16-byte Ghidra-seeded fragment that begins at LAB_004262d8, already inside 0x00426794, and repeats that routine's list-walk and Battle_UnitList_SetActorsFloatParam tail.
evidence: Damaged: the body is a byte-for-byte duplicate prefix of 0x00426794 with unaff_ registers, no callers and no callees of its own; it should eventually be merged into 0x00426794 rather than named.

name: Battle_RollHitRateByTemplate
signature: u32 Battle_RollHitRateByTemplate(void* actionTemplate, u32 actionIndex, u32 unitArg)
summary: Builds the eight-entry (0x2C stride) combat-modifier template of an action, finds the entry whose kind byte (+0x58) is 0x1D, turns it into a chance value with Battle_ResolveMemberCombatModifiers and returns 1 when a battle-RNG roll in [1,100] is at or below that chance.
evidence: Caller Battle_ActionSequence_DispatchActorState (0x003C583C) is confirmed battle-sequence code, the roll goes through the battle RNG at +0x4218 (func_001CA474, FACTS), and the entry kind 0x1D plus the 8x0x2C template layout are visible; only the exact meaning of kind 0x1D stays a description.

name: maybe_Camera_RegularShake_CreateWork
signature: void maybe_Camera_RegularShake_CreateWork(u32 heapId, u32 shakeParam0, u32 shakeParam1, u32 shakeParam2, u32 shakeParam3, u32 mode)
summary: Creates and registers a camera 'regular shake' work object: allocates 0x94 bytes from the memory manager, constructs it with the name-hash ctor (vtable 0x00591360 / g_cameraShakeWorkVtable), stores the four shake parameters and the mode byte, and inserts it into the named map at (work+8)->+0x78.
evidence: The old 'literal pool, not code' verdict is wrong: the shown body (Mem_AllocAligned_2(0x94), Container_NameHash_Ctor, Container_NamedMap_Insert on work+0x78) is real code, but the symbol starts ~0x18 bytes early - the 'ReguralyShake' key string sits at 0x00591204 and the push {r4,lr} of the real body is at 0x0059121C - so Ghidra decoded from inside the preceding literal pool. Class attribution comes from the neighbouring Camera_CreateRegularShakeWork / Camera_RegularShake_Ctor family, hence maybe_.

name: Sys_InitRenderSession
signature: void Sys_InitRenderSession(void* session, u32 unknown2, u32 screenParam3, u32 screenParam4, int padMask)
summary: Initialises a per-screen render/sound session: fills the two 0x100-entry command rings (+0x35C and +0x790, entries at +0x860 stride), starts the sound mixing state and the gfx command ring once per 3DS screen, stores the screen parameters and finally builds the 16-entry pad-button mask mapping.
evidence: The body calls Snd_InitMixingState and Gfx_InitCommandRing once for each of two rings, loops 0x100 times pushing entry pointers, then runs the same 16-button mask block that also exists as the separate fragment 0x00108F22; the old name described only the ring half of an initialiser that also brings up sound and input.

name: maybe_Input_UpdatePadStateThumb
signature: void maybe_Input_UpdatePadStateThumb(int mode, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6, u32 arg7, u32 arg8)
summary: Thumb-mode copy of the pad mapping block: reads Input_ReadPadState, maps the raw held/trigger masks through the 16-word button table into the output words and posts them; the argument list is unrecoverable.
evidence: Damaged 16-byte Thumb body (unaff_r5/r7/r9/r11, in_s0) with the identical constant sequence and the same func_00112448/func_00112450 helpers as the pad block at the end of 0x00108C5C, so only the shared block is certain; the Ghidra argument order and count are invented.

name: maybe_Gfx_CommandListWorker
signature: void maybe_Gfx_CommandListWorker(u32 arg1, u32 mask, int count, u32* d, int header, int* state)
summary: Normalises a command-list state counter modulo 8 and, when the list header/count are valid, stores a payload word into the list entry; the flow stops at a bad instruction, so only the header check and the modulo-8 normalisation are readable.
evidence: Damaged: the body contains 'Bad instruction - Truncating control flow' plus halt_baddata() and coprocessor_function() calls, and its only listed caller (Input_ReadPadState 0x0010C2D4) is a table neighbour rather than a real call, so even the Gfx prefix is unproven.

name: maybe_Battle_MessageQueue_PushWhenActorIdle
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_MessageQueue_PushWhenActorIdle(void* self, int* entry, int argument, u32 argument2)
summary: Deferred message push: keeps its own small state slot/timer on self and only when the acting battle unit is gone or Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty reports idle does it hand the prepared message entry to Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry (msgId taken from the dm row 0x1B family), so the popup is not queued while the unit is still animating.
evidence: The decisive callee is Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry (0x003FBE4C) together with Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty (0x00640348); per FACTS that pair is the battle message queue, not an effect or balloon spawner, so 'Ui_SpawnEventBalloon' invented a class that appears nowhere in the body.

name: Field_PlayOverlayStateSe
summary: Plays the sound effect that belongs to the current field overlay state: checks that the object's vtable class is g_playerActor3DClass, reads the overlay manager mode byte at (work+8)->+0x48 +0x281, resolves the state row with func_0063D6B8 and plays row+0x59 (or index 0xF for state 3 with byte +0x312 == 2) through Sound_PlaySeFromTable.
evidence: The +0x281 overlay mode byte is the documented UI overlay manager byte (FACTS: work+0x48 UI overlay manager), and the class comparison with g_playerActor3DClass shows the argument is a field actor; there is no window setup of any kind, so the old Ui_/window reading was wrong.

name: maybe_Item_SyncBagCountsFromList
summary: Walks a byte list of record ids, resolves each row with func_0063D338, keeps only rows of kind 8 whose id is not 0xFFFF and whose stored count differs from the bag's per-id count byte at (work+0x24A98)+id+0x2A70, then writes the count through the bag vtable slot +8 and registers a 0x1C-byte entry.
evidence: The body walks the ItemBag at work+0x24A98 (FACTS) and the per-id count bytes at bag+0x2A70, so this is bag/inventory synchronisation, not a UI 'object table'; the entry list owner and the meaning of row kind 8 remain unproven, and both callers are unnamed.

name: maybe_Actor_PlaySeFromActionTable
summary: Plays the SE attached to the actor's current action-table row: indexes the table at dm+0x3E4 with the actor's f_120 (0xC stride), resolves the sub-record with func_0062B540 from the row byte +4 and plays its SE id (+0x18) with the actor's f_170 as the volume/pan argument.
evidence: The whole body ends in Sound_PlaySeFromTableById and only reads an SE id out of the table row, so nothing 'plays an action'; the actor attribution rests on the self layout (f_120/f_160/f_170) and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Ui_BuildListEntries
summary: Builds one 0x84-byte text/icon entry per 0xC-stride row of the table returned by func_0063F0B8(tableId): copies the row name with std_wcsncpy, takes the icon id from row byte +5 and centres the glyph run before appending the entry.
evidence: The row table, the 0x84-byte entry records and the name/icon copy are explicit, but there are no callers and no string or record kind identifies which list this fills, so the Ui_ prefix and 'list entries' stay a description.

name: maybe_Data_SelectRecordIdByWeight
summary: Weighted random pick used by field gimmick setup: takes the id range spec[0]..spec[2], clamps it against the table returned by func_0064005C (count at +0x60), draws random values with std_FastSinCos and compares them with the per-row weights, returning the chosen record id.
evidence: Both callers are field gimmick setup (Field_Gimmick3107_SetupDrawObjectFromDesc 0x004B081C and maybe_Field_ModelSlotEmitter_InitFromDef 0x004B2CA4), which supports the weighted-choice reading of the float comparisons; the 1204-byte body is heavily restructured by Ghidra, so the record/weight layout stays inferred.

name: Model_SetupFromTypeId
summary: Type-id dependent model setup for a battle unit model: randomises the equip slots, for type 0x5A copies the param block and rolls a value from the battle RNG into self+0x28C, rebinds up to 32 sub-model slots when Battle_IsUnitModelVisible passes, and for type 0x116 stores the height difference against the data row's +0x28.
evidence: The body is fully readable and does exactly type-id-keyed setup on a model object (vtable +0xE8/+0xE4 sub-model rebinding, func_0058FC38 Model_CopyParamBlock, func_001CA474 on the battle RNG); the name is deliberately generic because no caller shows which unit kind uses each branch.

name: maybe_Field_LoadAreaActorData
summary: Loads the actor rows of one map area: scans the 0x14-byte rows of the dm actor table (func_0063D420) for the row with type byte 0xFF whose +2 is the current map id and whose +4 equals areaId, caches the match in the work words and rebuilds the per-cell actor entries for 0x36 cells with 9 sub-slots each.
evidence: No direct caller (the address is reached through a table), so the loader role is read purely from the loops: 0x14-stride rows keyed by map id + area id and the 0x36-cell rebuild. The 'area actor' wording is therefore still a description of the loops.

name: maybe_Field_CreateEncounterTrigger
summary: Builds the encounter trigger child of a field actor: looks up the enemy row by the actor's monster id (u16 at +0x258) with func_0063EEAC, allocates a 0x50-byte descriptor and attaches it to the actor's sprite through Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC using the 'shortRange'/'battle' names from the literal pool.
evidence: The 'battle' and 'shortRange' literals together with the enemy-row lookup by monster id are the DQXI encounter-trigger setup; somewhat weakened by the child being built through a vtable in the 0x77B190 Ui3D family, so the created object type is still uncertain.

name: maybe_Item_GetFirstOwnedVariant
summary: Resolves a row with func_0063D338 and returns the first of its four variant ids (+0x12/+0x14/+0x16/+0x18) that the save currently owns (probed with Item_RemoveFromParty, whose result is used as the ownership test), or 0xFFFF when none is owned.
evidence: The four-id fallback with the 0xFFFF sentinel is clear, and the probe callee Item_RemoveFromParty (0x0035F110) is a confirmed item function, so this is item-variant/present-in-party code; 'Valid' in the old name was undefined, and the sole caller is itself a maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_HasValidInteractTarget
summary: Returns 1 when the current interaction target (work+8 -> +0x88 -> +8) exists and is usable: either its kind byte +0x1C is 'x', or its id at +0x14 resolves through func_0063E070 to a row whose byte +4 is not 0xFF.
evidence: Returns a value (u32), so it is a real predicate and not a void stub with a dropped result; the only caller is a UI item panel (Ui_ItemPanel_RefreshFromConditions 0x0028AB10), which keeps the 'field interaction' label unproven even though the target slot at work+8->+0x88 is correct.

name: maybe_Model_ApplyParamType5
summary: For a type-0x5A model, copies the actor param block, finds the entry whose type byte is 5, rolls 1..100 on the battle RNG and, when the roll reaches the entry's threshold and model+0x3A5 is still empty, stores the caller's value there.
evidence: The siblings 0x001CBE54 (type 6) and 0x001CBF58 (type 4) show this is one member of a small family that applies the param entry of a given type; the old 'ApplyAttachPointParam' invented an attachment meaning that the code never mentions.

name: Model_ApplyParamType6
signature: void Model_ApplyParamType6(void* model, u32 spellId, int value)
